name: The speaker's card while music plays

pages.name: A speaker's card with a song on it

artboards.title: Today: the speaker's card while music plays, on a phone
A: the cover beside the words, on the cover blurred
B: everything on the cover, blurred
C: the cover stays, the sounds move below it

annotations.text:
WHY THIS EXISTS

20 November 2026, a song on the living room's HomePods: the cover is the whole card, sharp, and the words, the controls and eight sounds with a timer sit on top of it. On a bright cover the artist and the sounds wash out; on a portrait the chips sit on a face. And the card's name sits under the song's title.

IN EVERY DIRECTION

The card's name sits above the title. Every word on the card is held to the readable measure (e2e/readable.ts) with a bright cover and a dark one. A quiet speaker's card -- no song, the sounds offered -- is not changed here.

A: THE COVER BESIDE THE WORDS

The cover is a square beside the title, and behind the card is the same cover blurred and dimmed -- the resting TV's record (D), small. While music plays the card is the song: back, pause, next, where it is in the song, and the volume. The sounds are a quiet speaker's, and come back when it stops.

FOR: one way to show a record on every screen; the cover is seen whole, never under a chip.

AGAINST: the cover is small.

B: EVERYTHING ON THE COVER, BLURRED

The card keeps everything it has today, sounds included, on the cover blurred and dimmed.

FOR: the smallest change.

AGAINST: the cover itself is never seen sharp, and the sounds still crowd a song.

C: THE COVER STAYS, THE SOUNDS MOVE BELOW

The cover stays the card, sharp, with a shade across its top for the words; the sounds leave the card for a row under it.

FOR: the cover is as big as today.

AGAINST: a bright cover still pushes the shade dark, and the sounds are a second thing under every playing speaker.

PICK ONE

A (recommended), B, C, a mix, or something else -- describe it.
